import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Apex graphs and Jørgensen's conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Apex graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/apex_graph)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Jø94] Jørgensen, L. K., *Contractions to $K_8$*. J. Graph Theory 18 (1994), 431–448.
- [KNTW12] Kawarabayashi, K., Norine, S., Thomas, R., Wollan, P.,
  *$K_6$ minors in large 6-connected graphs*. [arXiv:1203.2192](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2192)

An *apex graph* is a graph that can be made planar by the removal of a single vertex.
Jørgensen conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an apex graph.
Kawarabayashi, Norine, Thomas and Wollan proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large
graphs, so a false conjecture would have only finitely many counterexamples.

Mathlib has neither planarity nor graph minors, so this file defines both. Planarity is defined
by a drawing in the plane without crossings, and a minor is defined by branch sets.
-/
namespace ApexGraph
open SimpleGraph unitInterval
open scoped EuclideanGeometry
variable {V W : Type*}

blocks.code:
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → ℝ²) (γ : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e, Continuous (γ e) ∧ Function.Injective (γ e)) ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, s(γ e 0, γ e 1) = (e : Sym2 V).map f) ∧
    (∀ e, ∀ t, t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 1 → γ e t ∉ Set.range f) ∧
    (∀ e e', e ≠ e' → ∀ t t', t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 1 → γ e t ≠ γ e' t')
blocks.docstring:
A graph `G` is *planar* if it has a drawing in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$: the vertices are
sent to distinct points and each edge is sent to an arc (an injective continuous image of the unit
interval) joining the images of its two ends. The interior of an arc contains no vertex, and the
interior of an arc meets no other arc. Two distinct arcs thus meet only in common endpoints.

By Wagner's theorem a finite graph is planar in this sense exactly when it has neither $K_5$
nor $K_{3,3}$ as a minor.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.UnitDistanceEmbeddable` / `UnitDistancePlaneGraph` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib (only place vertices in ℝ², no edge arcs or crossing conditions); Mathlib `Path`/`unitInterval` used as building blocks.
justification.name: ApexGraph.IsPlanar
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of planar graph (only a mention in a Coloring docstring). Defined as existence of a plane embedding: injective vertex map into ℝ², one continuous injective arc per edge joining its two ends, arc interiors avoiding vertices and all other arcs.

blocks.code:
def IsApex (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, IsPlanar (G.induce {v}ᶜ)
blocks.docstring:
A graph `G` is an *apex graph* if it has a vertex `v` whose deletion leaves a planar graph.
Such a vertex is called an *apex* of `G`.

Wikipedia also counts the null graph (no vertices) as an apex graph. This definition does not,
but the two agree on every graph with a vertex, and in particular on every $6$-connected graph.

justification.name: ApexGraph.IsApex
justification.why_needed: 'Apex graph' is not in Mathlib or the repo: a vertex whose deletion (`G.induce {v}ᶜ`) leaves a planar graph.

blocks.name: IsApex
blocks.text:
/-- A graph `G` is an *apex graph* if it has a vertex `v` whose deletion leaves a planar graph.
Such a vertex is called an *apex* of `G`.

Wikipedia also counts the null graph (no vertices) as an apex graph. This definition does not,
but the two agree on every graph with a vertex, and in particular on every $6$-connected graph. -/
def IsApex (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, IsPlanar (G.induce {v}ᶜ)

blocks.code:
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (B w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' ↦ Disjoint (B w) (B w')) ∧
    ∀ w w', H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ B w, ∃ v ∈ B w', G.Adj u v
blocks.docstring:
The graph `H` is a *minor* of the graph `G` if `H` can be obtained from a subgraph of `G` by
contracting edges. Equivalently, and this is the form used here, there are *branch sets*
`B w ⊆ V(G)` for `w ∈ V(H)` which are pairwise disjoint and each induce a connected (hence
nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that for every edge `w w'` of `H` some edge of `G` joins `B w`
to `B w'`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Matroid.IsMinor` (matroids, not graphs); `SimpleGraph.Subgraph`, `SimpleGraph.IsContained`/`⊑` (subgraph containment only, no contraction); `SimpleGraph.Connected` and `SimpleGraph.induce` are used as building blocks.
justification.name: ApexGraph.IsMinor
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has matroid minors but no graph minors. Defined via the standard branch-set (inflated subgraph) model: pairwise disjoint connected branch sets with an edge of G between the branch sets of every adjacent pair of H.

blocks.name: IsMinor
blocks.text:
/-- The graph `H` is a *minor* of the graph `G` if `H` can be obtained from a subgraph of `G` by
contracting edges. Equivalently, and this is the form used here, there are *branch sets*
`B w ⊆ V(G)` for `w ∈ V(H)` which are pairwise disjoint and each induce a connected (hence
nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that for every edge `w w'` of `H` some edge of `G` joins `B w`
to `B w'`. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (B w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' ↦ Disjoint (B w) (B w')) ∧
    ∀ w w', H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ B w, ∃ v ∈ B w', G.Adj u v

theorem apex_graph [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (h₆ : IsKConnected G 6)

blocks.docstring:
**Jørgensen's conjecture** [Jø94]. Every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an apex
graph. That is, if a finite graph $G$ has more than $6$ vertices, stays connected after the
deletion of any set of fewer than $6$ vertices, and does not contain the complete graph $K_6$ as
a minor, then $G$ has a vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph.

Kawarabayashi, Norine, Thomas and Wollan [KNTW12] proved the conjecture for all sufficiently
large graphs, so a false conjecture would have only finitely many counterexamples.

Kawarabayashi, Norine, Thomas and Wollan [KNTW12] proved the conjecture for all sufficiently
large graphs, so a false conjecture would have only finitely many counterexamples. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem apex_graph [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (h₆ : IsKConnected G 6)
    (hK₆ : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G) : IsApex G := by
  sorry

theorem isPlanar_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsPlanar G := by
  have : IsEmpty G.edgeSet := ⟨fun e ↦ isEmptyElim (Quot.out e.1).1⟩
  exact ⟨isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim, Function.injective_of_subsingleton _,
    isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim⟩

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_completeGraph_fin_two : IsPlanar (completeGraph (Fin 2)) := by
  set p : ℝ² := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 with hp
  have hp0 : p ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ by simpa [hp] using congrArg (· 0) h
  have hinj : Function.Injective fun r : ℝ ↦ r • p := smul_left_injective ℝ hp0
  have hsub : Subsingleton (completeGraph (Fin 2)).edgeSet :=
    ⟨fun e e' ↦ Subtype.ext ((coe_edgeSet_completeGraph_fin_two e).trans
      (coe_edgeSet_completeGraph_fin_two e').symm)⟩
  refine ⟨fun i ↦ (i : ℝ) • p, fun _ t ↦ (t : ℝ) • p, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i j h
    exact Fin.ext (Nat.cast_injective (hinj h))
  · intro e
    exact ⟨by fun_prop, fun s t h ↦ Subtype.ext (hinj h)⟩
  · intro e
    rw [coe_edgeSet_completeGraph_fin_two e]
    simp
  · rintro e t ht0 ht1 ⟨i, hi⟩
    have := hinj hi
    fin_cases i
    · exact ht0 (Subtype.ext (by simpa using this.symm))
    · exact ht1 (Subtype.ext (by simpa using this.symm))
  · intro e e' h
    exact absurd (Subsingleton.elim e e') h

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.card_le [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {H : SimpleGraph W} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    (h : IsMinor H G) : Fintype.card W ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  obtain ⟨B, hconn, hdisj, -⟩ := h
  refine Fintype.card_le_of_injective (fun x ↦ ((hconn x).nonempty.some : V)) fun x y hxy ↦ ?_
  by_contra hne
  exact (hdisj hne).ne_of_mem (hconn x).nonempty.some.2 (hconn y).nonempty.some.2 hxy
blocks.docstring: A minor of a finite graph has at most as many vertices as the graph.
blocks.name: IsMinor.card_le

theorem IsMinor.card_le [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {H : SimpleGraph W} {G : SimpleGraph V}

  obtain ⟨B, hconn, hdisj, -⟩ := h
  refine Fintype.card_le_of_injective (fun x ↦ ((hconn x).nonempty.some : V)) fun x y hxy ↦ ?_
  by_contra hne
  exact (hdisj hne).ne_of_mem (hconn x).nonempty.some.2 (hconn y).nonempty.some.2 hxy

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop over finite graphs (simple graphs suffice: loops/multi-edges affect neither planarity, K_6-minor-freeness, nor vertex connectivity); '6-vertex-connected' means more than 6 vertices and connected after deleting any fewer than 6 vertices (cf. the repo's IsKConnected, which builds in the vertex-count condition and so excludes the vacuous null graph), 'apex' means some vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph, and Mathlib currently lacks planarity and graph-minor definitions, which would need to be supplied in FormalConjecturesForMathlib; the article's remark that a false conjecture has only finitely many counterexamples is the known Kawarabayashi–Norine–Thomas–Wollan theorem, not an additional question posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and state the same theorem shape (finite simple graph G, repo `IsKConnected G 6` = more than 6 vertices and connected after deleting any <6 vertices, no K_6 minor in the standard branch-set model, conclusion: some vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph), which matches the statement and the primary source (KNTW arXiv:1203.2192, Conj. 1). They differ only in the bespoke planarity definition: c01/c02/c05/c06/c08 define planarity via Wagner's forbidden-minor theorem (extensionally correct for finite graphs but a theorem rather than the definition), while c03/c04/c07 use the literal topological definition (Jordan-arc drawing in ℝ²). I chose c07's version: its five conditions (injective vertex placement, arcs = continuous injective images of the unit interval, endpoints match the edge ends, arc interiors avoid vertices, arc interiors avoid all other arcs) match Diestel's definition of a plane graph exactly, and its test lemmas (K_2 drawn as a segment, empty graph planar, K_6 minor of K_7) exercise the definitions nontrivially. Edits: replaced `⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 6)` with `completeGraph (Fin 6)` (definitionally equal), used the repo's scoped `ℝ²` notation (as in c04), added c04's `IsMinor.card_le` / `not_isMinor_completeGraph_six` API tests, and dropped c07's extra `apex_graph.variants.large` (KNTW Theorem 1.1) since it is not a slot in the decomposition table.
claims.source_text: every 6-vertex-connected $K_6$-minor-free graph is an apex graph
claims.text_span: every 6-vertex-connected $K_6$-minor-free graph is an apex graph

context:
In graph theory, a branch of mathematics, an apex graph is a graph that can be made planar by the removal of a single vertex. The deleted vertex is called an apex of the graph. It is an apex, not the apex because an apex graph may have more than one apex; for example, in the minimal nonplanar graphs K5 or K3,3, every vertex is an apex. The apex graphs include graphs that are themselves planar, in which case again every vertex is an apex. The null graph is also counted as an apex graph even though it has no vertex to remove.
Apex graphs are closed under the operation of taking minors and play a role in several other aspects of graph minor theory: linkless embedding, Hadwiger's conjecture, YΔY-reducible graphs, and relations between treewidth and graph diameter.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition is right: the list entry is one universally quantified proposition, and the finiteness-of-counterexamples remark is the KNTW theorem (recorded only as a solved variant, not as a slot).

/-!

*References:*

An *apex graph* is a graph that can be made planar by the removal of a single vertex.
Jørgensen conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an apex graph.
Kawarabayashi, Norine, Thomas and Wollan proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large

Mathlib has neither planarity nor graph minors, so this file defines both. Planarity is defined

namespace ApexGraph

open SimpleGraph unitInterval
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- A graph `G` is *planar* if it has a drawing in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$: the vertices are
sent to distinct points and each edge is sent to an arc (an injective continuous image of the unit
interval) joining the images of its two ends. The interior of an arc contains no vertex, and the
interior of an arc meets no other arc. Two distinct arcs thus meet only in common endpoints.

By Wagner's theorem a finite graph is planar in this sense exactly when it has neither $K_5$
nor $K_{3,3}$ as a minor. -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → ℝ²) (γ : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e, Continuous (γ e) ∧ Function.Injective (γ e)) ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, s(γ e 0, γ e 1) = (e : Sym2 V).map f) ∧
    (∀ e, ∀ t, t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 1 → γ e t ∉ Set.range f) ∧
    (∀ e e', e ≠ e' → ∀ t t', t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 1 → γ e t ≠ γ e' t')

/-- A graph `G` is an *apex graph* if it has a vertex `v` whose deletion leaves a planar graph.
Such a vertex is called an *apex* of `G`.

Wikipedia also counts the null graph (no vertices) as an apex graph. This definition does not,
but the two agree on every graph with a vertex, and in particular on every $6$-connected graph. -/
def IsApex (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, IsPlanar (G.induce {v}ᶜ)

/-- The graph `H` is a *minor* of the graph `G` if `H` can be obtained from a subgraph of `G` by
contracting edges. Equivalently, and this is the form used here, there are *branch sets*
`B w ⊆ V(G)` for `w ∈ V(H)` which are pairwise disjoint and each induce a connected (hence
nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that for every edge `w w'` of `H` some edge of `G` joins `B w`
to `B w'`. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (B w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' ↦ Disjoint (B w) (B w')) ∧
    ∀ w w', H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ B w, ∃ v ∈ B w', G.Adj u v

/-- **Jørgensen's conjecture** [Jø94]. Every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an apex
graph. That is, if a finite graph $G$ has more than $6$ vertices, stays connected after the
deletion of any set of fewer than $6$ vertices, and does not contain the complete graph $K_6$ as
a minor, then $G$ has a vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph.

Kawarabayashi, Norine, Thomas and Wollan [KNTW12] proved the conjecture for all sufficiently
large graphs, so a false conjecture would have only finitely many counterexamples. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem apex_graph [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (h₆ : IsKConnected G 6)
    (hK₆ : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G) : IsApex G := by
  sorry

/-- A graph with no vertices is planar. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsPlanar G := by
  have : IsEmpty G.edgeSet := ⟨fun e ↦ isEmptyElim (Quot.out e.1).1⟩
  exact ⟨isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim, Function.injective_of_subsingleton _,
    isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim, isEmptyElim⟩

/-- The only edge of the complete graph on two vertices is `s(0, 1)`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
private lemma coe_edgeSet_completeGraph_fin_two (e : (completeGraph (Fin 2)).edgeSet) :
    (e : Sym2 (Fin 2)) = s(0, 1) := by
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := e
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h a b =>
    simp only [completeGraph, mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
    fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]

/-- A single edge is planar: draw it as the segment from `0` to `p` for a nonzero vector `p`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_completeGraph_fin_two : IsPlanar (completeGraph (Fin 2)) := by
  set p : ℝ² := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 with hp
  have hp0 : p ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ by simpa [hp] using congrArg (· 0) h
  have hinj : Function.Injective fun r : ℝ ↦ r • p := smul_left_injective ℝ hp0
  have hsub : Subsingleton (completeGraph (Fin 2)).edgeSet :=
    ⟨fun e e' ↦ Subtype.ext ((coe_edgeSet_completeGraph_fin_two e).trans
      (coe_edgeSet_completeGraph_fin_two e').symm)⟩
  refine ⟨fun i ↦ (i : ℝ) • p, fun _ t ↦ (t : ℝ) • p, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i j h
    exact Fin.ext (Nat.cast_injective (hinj h))
  · intro e
    exact ⟨by fun_prop, fun s t h ↦ Subtype.ext (hinj h)⟩
  · intro e
    rw [coe_edgeSet_completeGraph_fin_two e]
    simp
  · rintro e t ht0 ht1 ⟨i, hi⟩
    have := hinj hi
    fin_cases i
    · exact ht0 (Subtype.ext (by simpa using this.symm))
    · exact ht1 (Subtype.ext (by simpa using this.symm))
  · intro e e' h
    exact absurd (Subsingleton.elim e e') h

/-- A graph with exactly one vertex is an apex graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isApex_of_unique [Unique V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsApex G :=
  haveI : IsEmpty ({default}ᶜ : Set V) :=
    ⟨fun ⟨v, hv⟩ ↦ hv (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mpr (Subsingleton.elim v default))⟩
  ⟨default, isPlanar_of_isEmpty _⟩

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  ⟨fun v ↦ {v}, fun v ↦ by simp,
    fun _ _ h ↦ Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr h,
    fun u v h ↦ ⟨u, rfl, v, rfl, h⟩⟩

/-- A minor of a finite graph has at most as many vertices as the graph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.card_le [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {H : SimpleGraph W} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    (h : IsMinor H G) : Fintype.card W ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  obtain ⟨B, hconn, hdisj, -⟩ := h
  refine Fintype.card_le_of_injective (fun x ↦ ((hconn x).nonempty.some : V)) fun x y hxy ↦ ?_
  by_contra hne
  exact (hdisj hne).ne_of_mem (hconn x).nonempty.some.2 (hconn y).nonempty.some.2 hxy

/-- A graph with fewer than `6` vertices has no `K₆` minor. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isMinor_completeGraph_six [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (hV : Fintype.card V < 6) :
    ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G := fun h ↦ by
  have := h.card_le
  simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at this
  omega

/-- The complete graph $K_6$ is a minor of $K_7$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_six_completeGraph_seven :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) (completeGraph (Fin 7)) :=
  ⟨fun w ↦ {Fin.castSucc w}, fun w ↦ by simp,
    fun _ _ h ↦ Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr ((Fin.castSucc_injective _).ne h),
    fun u v h ↦ ⟨_, rfl, _, rfl, by simpa using h⟩⟩

end ApexGraph

items: Graphs are finite simple graphs (`SimpleGraph V` with `[Fintype V]`); loops and multiple edges do not affect 6-connectivity, K_6-minor-freeness, or planarity, matching the decomposition notes.

'6-vertex-connected' is the repo's `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 6`: `6 < Fintype.card V` and `G.induce Sᶜ` connected for every finset `S` with `S.card < 6` (Diestel's definition; excludes the null graph and graphs on ≤ 6 vertices).

Planarity is defined topologically (`IsPlanar`): an injective map of vertices into `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` and, for each edge, a continuous injective map from the unit interval whose two endpoints are the images of the edge's ends (expressed with `Sym2.map`), such that interior points of an arc are not vertices and interior points of an arc lie on no other arc. This is the textbook definition of a plane embedding; the Kuratowski/Wagner minor characterisation was deliberately NOT used as the definition (it is mentioned in the docstring only as an equivalence).

Minors are defined via branch sets (`IsMinor H G`): pairwise disjoint vertex sets `B w` (w a vertex of H) each inducing a connected — hence nonempty — subgraph of G, with an edge of G between `B w` and `B w'` for every edge `w w'` of H. This is Diestel's IH characterisation, equivalent to 'obtained from a subgraph by contracting edges'. K_6 is `(⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 6))`, so isomorphism is built in.

`IsApex G := ∃ v, IsPlanar (G.induce {v}ᶜ)`. This differs from Wikipedia's convention only on the null graph (Wikipedia counts it as apex); irrelevant here because 6-connected graphs have at least 7 vertices. Documented in the docstring.
Argument order `IsMinor H G` means 'H is a minor of G', following Mathlib's `Matroid.IsMinor N M` convention.

An extra declaration `apex_graph.variants.large` (category research solved) records the Kawarabayashi–Norine–Thomas–Wollan theorem (Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:1203.2192): ∃ N, every 6-connected K_6-minor-free graph on ≥ N vertices is apex. It is a variant, not a slot, added per the repo convention of keeping closely related variants in the same file.

Bespoke definitions live in the problem file rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib because the sandbox only permits writing the single candidate file; a reviewer may wish to move `IsPlanar`/`IsMinor` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/ as reusable definitions.

Test/API lemmas with full proofs check the definitions on small cases: empty graph is planar, a single edge (K_2) is planar via an explicit straight-line drawing, a one-vertex graph is apex, `IsMinor` is reflexive, and K_6 is a minor of K_7.

reviewer_notes: Statement is a single universally quantified Prop; no ambiguity beyond the modeling choices already fixed by the decomposition table (finite simple graphs; repo IsKConnected; apex = ∃ vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph). The null-graph convention for apex graphs is irrelevant because IsKConnected G 6 forces |V| > 6; this is noted in the IsApex docstring. Loops/multi-edges (allowed by KNTW) affect none of the three properties, so SimpleGraph is faithful. Verified `completeGraph V = ⊤` by rfl and printed the elaborated main theorem: `∀ {V} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsKConnected 6 → ¬IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G → IsApex G`. Bespoke definitions (IsPlanar, IsApex, IsMinor) live in the problem file because only a single output file is permitted; maintainers may prefer to move IsPlanar/IsMinor to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/. The Wagner-based candidates (c01, c02, c05, c06, c08) are also faithful (equivalent for finite graphs); c08's redundant `IsPlanar G ∨` disjunct in IsApex is harmless.
